document_metadata.document_title: Illinois Model Stormwater Management Ordinance (capital MS4 template reference)

design_criteria.water_quality_volume_method: IL Model Stormwater Management Ordinance / Illinois Urban Manual BMP framework. Site runoff controls for large storms through the 100-year event with post-development discharge rates not exceeding pre-development for specified events. Minor storm sewers/inlets/swales designed for the 10-year critical duration storm; BMPs per Illinois Urban Manual.
peak_flow_calculation_method: Hydrologic methods allowed by ordinance (e.g., HEC-HMS)

10-year critical duration storm shall be used as a minimum for the design of storm sewers, storm inlets, and minor swales
The basin must be designed to dewater within 72 hours following the end of the 100-year critical duration storm event.
The bottom of the infiltration basin must be at least four (4) feet above the seasonal high groundwater elevation.
The underlying soils must have an infiltration rate of at least 0.5 inches per hour as determined by an engineer.
A minimum depth of 24 inches between the bottom of the facility and the infiltration horizon

For new permeable pavement, designers should use one-half of the measured infiltration rate during design
Approaches may include green roofs, naturalized detention facilities, trees and tree boxes, rain gardens, vegetated swales

extraction_quality.review_notes: Placeholder statewide model ordinance — replace when City of Springfield publishes a local drainage/stormwater design manual PDF.

design_parameters.enrich_notes: Source is IDNR/OWR Model Stormwater Management Ordinance (Springfield placeholder). BMP design details defer to Illinois Urban Manual (Oct 2013). Appendix A credits use 0.25 inch runoff depth for non-structural volume reduction, not stated as a standalone WQV design depth. Infiltration BMPs require 24 inches minimum between facility bottom and infiltration horizon (505.2.A), distinct from 4 ft seasonal high groundwater separation for infiltration basins.
